import java.util.*

fun main() {
    val sc = Scanner(System.`in`)
    val n = sc.nextInt()
    val t = sc.nextInt()
    val memo = HashMap<State, Long>()
    println(count(1, 0, 0, 0, n, t, memo))
}

data class State(val pos: Int, val prevY: Int, val peaks: Int, val valleys: Int)

fun count(pos: Int, prevY: Int, peaks: Int, valleys: Int, n: Int, t: Int, memo: HashMap<State, Long>): Long {
    if (peaks > t || valleys > t - 1) return 0L
    if (pos == n) {
        return if (peaks == t && valleys == t - 1) 1L else 0L
    }
    val key = State(pos, prevY, peaks, valleys)
    if (memo.containsKey(key)) return memo[key]!!
    var res = 0L
    for (y in 1..4) {
        if (y == prevY) continue
        var newPeaks = peaks
        var newValleys = valleys
        if (pos >= 2) {
            val prevPrevY = prevY
            val currY = y
            if (prevPrevY < prevY && prevY > currY) newPeaks++
            if (prevPrevY > prevY && prevY < currY) newValleys++
        }
        res += count(pos + 1, y, newPeaks, newValleys, n, t, memo)
    }
    memo[key] = res
    return res
}
